name: Indiana
feeText: Total civil filing fees $157: civil filing fee $100 (IC 33-37-4-4(a)) + document storage $5 + automated record keeping $20 + public defense administration $5 + judicial insurance adjustment $1 + judicial salaries $20 + court administration $5 + pro bono services $1 (Indiana Trial Court Fee Manual, current through the 2026 legislative session). $185 where the clerk also collects the $28 sheriff's service fee.

otherFees.what: Alternative dispute resolution fee on a petition for dissolution, in counties with an approved ADR plan (IC 33-23-6-1)
Sheriff's service of process fee, where collected by the clerk

residency.text: At least one party must have been an Indiana resident (or stationed at a US military installation in Indiana) for six months, and a resident of the county of filing for three months, immediately before filing (IC 31-15-2-6).

waitingPeriod.text: The final hearing may not be held earlier than 60 days after the petition is filed (IC 31-15-2-10); a summary decree also requires at least 60 days (IC 31-15-2-13).

simplified.text: Summary dissolution decree without a final hearing at least 60 days after filing, on verified pleadings signed by both parties with a written waiver of final hearing and either a statement of no contested issues or a written settlement agreement (IC 31-15-2-13).

parentingClass.text: No statewide parenting-class requirement found in IC Title 31 (2025 edition); requirements are set by county local rules.

uncertain: IC Title 31 (2025 edition) read from the Internet Archive copy (2025-11-13) of https://iga.in.gov/ic/2025/Title_31.html; iga.in.gov serves a script-only page to automated clients.
No answer/response fee is listed in the Indiana Trial Court Fee Manual civil table; responseFee left null.
Fee waiver (indigency) form not verified on in.gov/courts.
County local rules requiring parenting classes (e.g. Marion County) not checked.

name: Colorado
feeText: Docket fee paid by the petitioner in a proceeding for dissolution of marriage, legal separation or declaration of invalidity: $230; by the respondent: $116 (C.R.S. 13-32-101(1)(a) and (b)).

otherFees.what: Motion to modify, amend or alter a decree or order more than 60 days after the decree (C.R.S. 13-32-101(2), per JDF 1 fee chart)
Petition for allocation of parental responsibilities (per JDF 1 fee chart)

residency.text: One party must have been domiciled in Colorado for 91 days before the proceeding is commenced (C.R.S. 14-10-106(1)(a)(I)).

waitingPeriod.text: The decree may be entered only when 91 days or more have elapsed since the court acquired jurisdiction over the respondent (service, joining as co-petitioner, or appearance) (C.R.S. 14-10-106(1)(a)(III)).

simplified.text: Decree upon affidavit without a hearing when there are no minor children (or both parties are represented and have a separation agreement on children), the respondent is served, there is no genuine issue of material fact, and there is no marital property or the parties agree on its division (C.R.S. 14-10-120.3).

parentingClass.text: No statewide mandate in statute: a court may order a parent of a child under 18 to attend a parental education program on the impact of separation and divorce (C.R.S. 14-10-123.7(2)); judicial districts may require it by local practice.

uncertain: C.R.S. Titles 13 and 14 read from the Internet Archive copies (2026-09) of the 2024 uncertified printouts at content.leg.colorado.gov (direct access returned HTTP 403); the 2025 printout was not archived.
The JDF 1 fee chart (revision R2/14, posted 2023-08) matches the statutory $230 / $116; other amounts listed in otherFees are from that chart and may be outdated.
Fee waiver form (Colorado Judicial JDF form) not verified; coloradojudicial.gov fee page returned 404.
Whether each judicial district (e.g. Denver, El Paso) makes the parenting class mandatory by local rule not checked.

name: Oregon
feeText: Dissolution of marriage, annulment or separation: $301 for the first appearance by petitioner, respondent or other party (ORS 21.155(1)), Oregon circuit court fee schedule effective 2026-01-01.

waiver.name: Fee Deferral and Waiver packet (Oregon Judicial Department Forms Center)

residency.text: If the marriage was solemnized in Oregon and the ground is irreconcilable differences, either party must be a resident or domiciliary when the suit is filed; otherwise at least one party must have been a resident or domiciliary for six months before filing (ORS 107.075).

waitingPeriod.text: No statutory waiting period found in ORS chapter 107; the marriage is terminated when the court signs the judgment of dissolution (ORS 107.115(2)).

simplified.text: Summary dissolution (ORS 107.485): no children of the marriage and no pregnancy, marriage of 10 years or less, no real property, unpaid debts since marriage of $15,000 or less, personal property under $30,000 net, petitioner waives spousal support and pendente lite orders, no other pending domestic relations suit.

uncertain: ORS chapters 107 and 21 were read from the Internet Archive 2026 copy of oregonlegislature.gov (direct fetch failed on 2026-10-08).
Parenting education: ORS 3.425 (county parent education programs) could not be fetched (oregonlegislature.gov ors003.html unavailable directly and in the archive); required = null.
Exact title of the Oregon fee deferral/waiver application form not readable (forms list loads by script); the fees page refers to the 'fee deferral or waiver packet'.
Waiting period 0 inferred from the absence of any waiting-period provision in ORS chapter 107 text searched; no explicit statement 'no waiting period' exists in statute.

name: Rhode Island

otherFees.what: eFileRI one-time civil case processing fee to Tyler Technologies, in addition to the court filing fee (revised March 2026)

residency.text: The plaintiff must have been domiciled in and resided in Rhode Island for one year before filing; satisfied instead if the defendant has been so domiciled for one year and is actually served (R.I. Gen. Laws § 15-5-12(a)).

waitingPeriod.text: No divorce judgment becomes final until three months after the trial and decision; the final decree may then be entered ex parte within 180 days (R.I. Gen. Laws § 15-5-23(a)).

simplified.text: No summary procedure found; a three-year separation ground leads to a decision pending entry of final judgment, which may be entered 20 days after the decision (R.I. Gen. Laws § 15-5-3).

uncertain: Family Court divorce filing fee not found: the courts.ri.gov fee documents found (Superior Court fees $160, eFileRI fees) do not cover the Family Court; filingFee null.
R.I. Gen. Laws §§ 15-5-12, 15-5-23 and 15-5-3 read from Internet Archive 2026 copies (webserver.rilegislature.gov refused connections on 2026-10-08).
waitingPeriod.days 90 stands for 'three months' after the decision (not after filing).
Irreconcilable differences ground (§ 15-5-3.1), fee waiver form and Family Court parent education requirement not verified.

name: South Carolina
feeText: Uniform fee of $100 for filing a first complaint or petition in a civil action (S.C. Code § 8-21-310(C)(1)) plus an additional $50 fee (S.C. Code § 14-1-204(B)(1)) = $150.

residency.text: The plaintiff must have resided in South Carolina for one year before filing (or, if the plaintiff is a nonresident, the defendant for one year); if both parties are residents when the action is filed, three months is enough (S.C. Code § 20-3-30).

waitingPeriod.text: No reference before two months after filing and no final decree before three months after filing; on the grounds of desertion or one-year separation the hearing and decree may follow the responsive pleadings or default (S.C. Code § 20-3-80).

separationText: No-fault ground: the spouses have lived separate and apart without cohabitation for one year (S.C. Code § 20-3-10(5)); fault grounds (adultery, desertion for one year, physical cruelty, habitual drunkenness) need no separation.

simplified.text: No summary dissolution procedure in Title 20, Chapter 3.

uncertain: waitingPeriod.days 90 stands for the statutory 'three months' after filing (§ 20-3-80); it does not apply to one-year-separation or desertion cases.
Answer/response fee: § 8-21-310(C)(1) says there is no further fee for other papers in the same action, but no explicit statement about the defendant's answer was read; responseFee left null.
Fee waiver (in forma pauperis) form and any Family Court parenting-class requirement not verified on sccourts.org.

name: South Dakota
feeText: Clerk of courts fee of $25 for civil cases filed for jury or court trial (SDCL 16-2-29(3)(a)) plus the $40 unified judicial system court automation surcharge in each civil action (SDCL 16-2-39) = $65.

otherFees.what: Petition or motion to modify final child support, custody, visitation or spousal support orders (SDCL 16-2-29(4))

waiver.name: Motion to waive filing fees and service costs with affidavit of inability to pay (SDCL 16-2-29.2, 16-2-29.3)

residency.text: The plaintiff must be a resident of South Dakota (or stationed there in the armed services) when the action is commenced; no minimum duration, and residence need not be maintained afterwards (SDCL 25-4-30).

waitingPeriod.text: A divorce may not be heard, tried or determined until at least 60 days after completed service of the summons and complaint (SDCL 25-4-34).

uncertain: Filing fee $65 is the sum of two statutes (SDCL 16-2-29(3) and 16-2-39) as read; whether divorce falls under 16-2-29(3)(a) or (k) is not stated, both are $25. The Unified Judicial System's own fee schedule could not be found to confirm the total actually collected.
No answer fee found in SDCL 16-2-29; responseFee left null.
Simplified procedure and parenting-class requirement not verified (SDCL ch. 25-4A standard guidelines and mediation under 25-4-56 read; no class mandate found in the sections read).

name: Utah
feeText: $350 for a petition for an action under Title 81, Chapter 4, Dissolution of Marriage (Utah Code § 78A-2-301(1)(b)(iv), version effective 2026-05-06).

otherFees.what: Counterclaim when the original petition is a dissolution of marriage action (§ 78A-2-301(1)(d)(iv))
Petition for temporary separation, credited toward the divorce fee (§ 78A-2-301(1)(b)(v))
Petition or counter-petition to modify a domestic relations order (§ 78A-2-301(1)(q))

waiver.name: Waiver of fees for indigent litigants on affidavit (Utah Code § 78A-2-302)

residency.text: The petitioner or the petitioner's spouse must have been an actual and bona fide resident of the county of filing for at least 90 days before filing, or the petitioner stationed in Utah under military orders for at least 90 days (Utah Code § 81-4-402(1)).

waitingPeriod.text: The court may not enter a decree of divorce until 30 days after the petition is filed, unless it finds extraordinary circumstances (Utah Code § 81-4-402(3)(a)).

simplified.text: No summary dissolution procedure found in Utah Code Title 81, Chapter 4.

parentingClass.text: Parties with a minor child must attend the mandatory divorce orientation course (§ 81-4-105, at least one hour) and the mandatory parenting course (§ 81-9-103): the petitioner within 60 days of filing and the respondent within 30 days of service; no decree until certificates are filed, unless waived by the court (§ 81-4-402(4)).

uncertain: Utah recodified its domestic relations law into Title 81 (effective 2024-09-01); former Title 30 sections are empty. Title 81 Chapter 4 was read from the chapter PDF version C81-4_2024090120240501, which includes amendments through the 2026 General Session.
Answer/response fee: § 78A-2-301 lists no fee for an answer as such; only a counterclaim fee ($130 when the original petition is a dissolution). responseFee left null.
§ 78A-2-301 has a version superseding it on 2027-01-01; the 2026-05-06 version was used.
Exact title of the Utah court fee-waiver form not verified (utcourts.gov pages returned 404/406); only the statute is cited.

name: Vermont
feeText: $295 before the entry of any divorce or annulment proceeding in the Superior Court; $90 if filed with a stipulation for a final order and one or both parties are residents ($180 if neither is a resident) (32 V.S.A. § 1431(b)(2)).

otherFees.what: Divorce complaint filed with a stipulation for a final order, at least one party resident (32 V.S.A. § 1431(b)(2))
Motion or petition to vacate or modify a child support order (32 V.S.A. § 1431(b)(5))

residency.text: A complaint may be brought if either party has resided in Vermont for six months or more, but no divorce may be decreed unless the plaintiff or defendant has resided in the State one year before the final hearing (15 V.S.A. § 592(a)).

waitingPeriod.text: A divorce decree is first a decree nisi and becomes absolute 90 days after entry, unless the court fixes an earlier date (15 V.S.A. § 554(a)).

separationText: No-fault ground: the spouses have lived apart for six consecutive months and resumption of marital relations is not reasonably probable (15 V.S.A. § 551(7)); fault grounds need no separation.

simplified.text: No separate summary procedure in statute; an uncontested complaint filed with a stipulation for a final order pays a reduced $90 fee (32 V.S.A. § 1431(b)(2)).

uncertain: Fee waiver form name/URL not verified: vermontjudiciary.org returned HTTP 403 to automated clients on 2026-10-08.
Parenting class requirement not verified (court rule / vermontjudiciary.org not readable).
No answer fee appears in 32 V.S.A. § 1431(b)(2); responseFee left null rather than 0 because the Vermont Judiciary fee schedule could not be read.
separationRequiredDays 182 is the day equivalent of 'six consecutive months' in § 551(7) and applies only to the no-fault ground.

name: West Virginia
feeText: Clerk of the circuit court fee for instituting an action for divorce, separate maintenance or annulment: $135 (W. Va. Code § 59-1-11(a)(3)).

otherFees.what: Petition to modify an order on custody, visitation, child support or spousal support (§ 59-1-11(a)(4))
Expedited modification of a child support order (§ 59-1-11(a)(5))
Parent education class fee, waived if indigent (§ 48-9-104(c)), maximum

residency.text: If married in West Virginia, one party must be a bona fide resident when the action is filed (no minimum duration); if married elsewhere, one party must have been a resident for the one year before filing (W. Va. Code § 48-5-105(a)).

simplified.text: Irreconcilable differences: divorce may be ordered when the complaint alleges irreconcilable differences and an answer admits it, without corroboration (W. Va. Code § 48-5-201). Alternatively, one year of living separate and apart is a ground (§ 48-5-202).

parentingClass.text: In a divorce involving a minor child the family court shall order the parties to attend parent education classes unless it finds attendance not appropriate or necessary; fee up to $25, waived for indigent parties (W. Va. Code § 48-9-104(b)-(c)).

uncertain: responseFee 0: § 59-1-11(a)(6) imposes a $200 fee on pleadings with a counterclaim but states it does not apply in family court cases; no answer fee is listed.

Waiting period not found in W. Va. Code ch. 48 art. 5 sections read (48-5-104 to 106, 201 to 203, 301); any minimum time is set by the Rules of Practice and Procedure for Family Court, not verified. days = null.
Fee waiver form (courtswv.gov) not verified.

name: Wisconsin
feeText: Commencing a family action (divorce, annulment, legal separation) with no request for support or maintenance: $184.50 ($75 filing fee, $68 CSS, $21.50 JINFO, $20 family court counseling services fee) (Wis. Stat. § 814.61(1)(a)-(b)); $194.50 with a request for support or maintenance (extra $10 under § 814.61(13)). Wisconsin Circuit Court Fee Tables updated November 14, 2024.

otherFees.what: Family action with a request for support or maintenance (§ 814.61(1)(b), (13))
E-filing fee per party when the case is electronically filed (§ 758.19(4m), 801.18(7))
Post-judgment motion in a family action (§ 814.61(7)(a))

waiver.name: Petition for waiver of fees and costs (Wis. Stat. § 814.29(1))

residency.text: One party must have been a bona fide resident of Wisconsin for at least 6 months and of the county of filing for at least 30 days before commencing a divorce (Wis. Stat. § 767.301).

waitingPeriod.text: A divorce may not be brought to final hearing or trial until 120 days after service of the summons and petition on the respondent, or 120 days after filing a joint petition, unless the court orders an immediate hearing for an emergency (Wis. Stat. § 767.335).

simplified.text: No summary dissolution procedure; spouses may file a joint petition, which starts the 120-day waiting period on the filing date (Wis. Stat. § 767.335(1)).

parentingClass.text: No statewide mandate in statute: in an action affecting the family with a minor child, the court may order the parties to attend a program (up to 4 hours) on the effects of dissolution on children (Wis. Stat. § 767.401(1)); counties may require it by local rule.

uncertain: docs.legis.wisconsin.gov refused connections on 2026-10-08; §§ 767.301 and 767.335 were read from the Internet Archive copy (2023-10-02) of /statutes/statutes/767/iv and § 767.401 from the 2026-06-11 copy of /767/v. Most populous county (Milwaukee) local rules not checked.
Fee table read from the Internet Archive copy (2026-07-01) of wicourts.gov/courts/circuit/docs/fees.pdf (direct access HTTP 403); table dated November 14, 2024 — a 2026 update was not found.
No answer/response fee appears in the family section of the fee table; responseFee left null.
Exact Wisconsin fee-waiver form number not verified; the statute (§ 814.29(1)) is cited.

name: Wyoming
feeText: District court clerk original filing fee for each civil action, paid by the plaintiff: $160, of which $40 is for court automation and $10 for indigent civil legal services (W.S. 5-3-206(a)(i)).

residency.text: One party must have resided in Wyoming for 60 days immediately before filing, or the marriage was solemnized in Wyoming and one party has resided there since the marriage (W.S. 20-2-107(a)).

waitingPeriod.text: A divorce decree shall not be entered less than 20 days from the date the complaint is filed (W.S. 20-2-108).

simplified.text: No summary dissolution procedure found in Wyoming Title 20; the only ground besides insanity is irreconcilable differences (W.S. 20-2-104).

parentingClass.text: No statewide mandate in statute: the court may at any time require parents to attend parenting classes, including classes to lessen the effects of divorce on children (W.S. 20-2-201(f)); individual judicial districts may require them by local rule.

uncertain: No answer/response fee appears in W.S. 5-3-206(a) (the original filing fee is paid by the plaintiff); responseFee left null.
Local district court rules on mandatory parenting classes not checked.
Fee waiver (in forma pauperis) form not verified on wyocourts.gov.
